title: Gavaskar Tells India's Batters to Take Responsibility After Hyderabad Loss
excerpt: Sunil Gavaskar praised Sanju Samson's start but criticised the batters who followed as India fell 24 runs short of West Indies' 247 in the fourth T20I.
body:
• Sunil Gavaskar said India's batting unit must show more responsibility in chases after the 24-run loss to West Indies in the fourth T20I in Hyderabad.
  • West Indies made 247 for 3, with Shai Hope 102 not out, and India replied with 223 for 9 despite Sanju Samson's 56 off 23 balls; Keemo Paul took 5 for 41.
  • Gavaskar praised Samson's start but criticised the batters who followed, while defending India's inexperienced bowlers.
  • The five-match series is level at 2-2, with the decider in Bengaluru on Saturday 17 October.

Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar has criticised India's batters for failing to take responsibility in a run chase, after West Indies beat India by 24 runs in the fourth T20 International in Hyderabad on Wednesday to level the five-match series at 2-2.

Speaking on JioStar after the match, Gavaskar said the first thing India must improve is how they chase. In a brief remark reported by The Times of India, he said the batting unit needs to show more responsibility, and warned that the side will not succeed if the batters do not take it.

"The batting unit needs to show more responsibility."

— Sunil Gavaskar, former India captain, on JioStar

A chase that started well and then stalled

West Indies, put in to bat, posted 247 for 3 in 20 overs. Captain Shai Hope finished unbeaten on 102 from 50 balls, with Sherfane Rutherford 49 not out, according to the ESPNcricinfo scorecard. India reached 223 for 9 in 19.3 overs, with Arshdeep Singh retiring hurt late in the chase.

Sanju Samson gave India the start Gavaskar wanted, scoring 56 from 23 balls. Gavaskar's complaint was about what followed. As reported by MyKhel in its coverage of the JioStar experts, he said the rest of the batting did not build on Samson's innings, pointed to Abhishek Sharma's dismissal, noted Ishan Kishan's failure to counter Keemo Paul's plan, and said Shreyas Iyer has struggled since his century earlier in the series.

Paul was the bowler who broke the chase, taking 5 for 41 in four overs. Gudakesh Motie took 2 for 13. Tilak Varma's 43 was India's next highest score after Samson.

Gavaskar defends the bowlers

Gavaskar was more forgiving of India's attack, which conceded 247. He argued, in the Times of India report, that the bowlers are new to international cricket and need to be allowed to learn, even if that means being hit for boundaries. The distinction matters: his criticism was aimed at an experienced batting group, not at a developing bowling unit.

MyKhel also reported Gavaskar's suggestion for the decider: that India should look to bat first in Bengaluru, aim for a total in the 240 to 250 range, and then defend it, rather than face another chase of this size.

What it means for the decider

The result, already covered in our match report, leaves the series tied at 2-2. The fifth T20I is in Bengaluru on Saturday 17 October, starting at 7pm IST, and will decide the series.

For India, Gavaskar's point sets the selection and tactics question plainly. Samson's form at the top is not the problem. The middle order's conversion in a chase is. If India chase again in Bengaluru, the batters Gavaskar named will be the ones under scrutiny from the first over.
